event.notes: "mode": "auto" means every run resolves this itself — before config.json is even loaded, it asks ESPN for the soonest upcoming card, and if that differs from "name" below it rewrites "name"/"league"/"date", regenerates discovery.title_contains and discovery.search.queries from the new main event's fighters, and clears tracker.picks_videos (a stale roundup URL would just burn a download and a vision pass on the old event's deck). Once this week's card has happened, the next run rolls to whatever's next on its own — no manual retarget. "name"/"league"/"date" below are simply the last-resolved event; edit them by hand only if you delete "mode" and want to pin a specific card again (e.g. a Contender Series week, matched as a substring against ESPN's own event name — punctuation and case ignored, spelling not). "league" pins which scoreboard is searched (ufc / pfl); leave it empty to try UFC then PFL. Add more cards to the top-level "events" array to cover them in the same run — a PFL event the same weekend, say — and the dashboard puts a card selector at the top. If a run logs "No ESPN card found" (or, in auto mode, "No upcoming event found"), something's off with the league or the scoreboard is unreachable — nothing is filtered and off-card fights come back.

sources.title: UFC Fight Night: Prochazka vs. Stirling

notes: Lightweight. Every one of Ortega's 15 method votes bar one is a submission, and the oddsmakers rate a Hooker KO (+210) a shade behind his decision (+180) despite only 18% of the field picking it.

tally_source.event_name: UFC Fight Night: Prochazka vs. Stirling

notes: Flyweight rematch — Albazi won the first by KO four years ago — and the closest fight on the card at -115/-105.
Close everywhere: 58% Costa in the field, the best predictors 3-3, the best underdog-pickers 4-4, and every best method predictor expecting a decision either way.
FLAG — the host gave the method split without stating its total, so the usual reconciliation check could not run; 54 is the sum of the counts he read out.
He called an Albazi decision the oddsmakers' likeliest outcome but gave no price, so no method price is recorded.

tally_source.event_name: UFC Fight Night: Prochazka vs. Stirling

notes: Light heavyweight main event, five rounds. Stirling is 11-0 and 6-0 in the UFC.
96% of the method votes have this ending by KO and not one channel picked a submission; the best method predictors split 2-2 on who lands it.

tally_source.event_name: UFC Fight Night: Prochazka vs. Stirling

notes: Heavyweight. 96% of the method votes are a KO either way, and not one of the 8 best underdog-pickers is on Teixeira.

The host's second best bet: every panel 100% on Gaziev and the KO at -140 against a -195 moneyline. He said the method predictors were unanimous on it too but gave no panel size, so no method-panel count is recorded.
